purpose: Labelled family-claim set for the pair-evidence mining experiment: reprocess Fourth Wing with the mining build and compare per-pair outcomes against the -13 baseline recorded here. Survival = the pair is present in the new run's relationships (i.e. NOT in dropped_relationships).
pair_form: from/to/type as stored in the -13 artefact (post-canonicalization; type describes `from`).
acceptance_signals: true_pairs survival (not dropped) UP vs baseline: baseline 2/5 survive (Brennan downgraded to 'other', Mira kept); target >= 4/5 survive, with parent types intact where the mined evidence is binding.

false_pairs survival ~ UNCHANGED vs baseline: baseline 0/13 survive (all dropped); mining must not resurrect them (target <= 1/13, and any survivor must be a downgrade to 'other', never the claimed family type).

evidence-less write skips DOWN: baseline 18 evidence-less relationships in preview; target <= 8 after mined write evidence (count via the run's 'Skipped N evidence-less relationships' line / _build_rel_map on the new artefact).

error_taxonomy.source: Error classes from the character-extraction literature, in this pipeline's terms. Used to label fixture failures so live-run results stay comparable across runs and against published work.
error_taxonomy.missing: A true pair or character the pipeline failed to produce in correct form: never extracted, dropped before write, or stripped of its true type in validation (e.g. a true sibling claim downgraded to 'other').
error_taxonomy.hallucinated: A claim the pipeline produced with no basis in the text: an invented relationship, type, or character that validation exists to kill before it is written.
error_taxonomy.false_merge: Two distinct characters collapsed into one roster entry (usually via a shared or mis-assigned alias), so both characters' claims and relationships land on a single identity.
error_taxonomy.false_split: One character split across two roster entries (e.g. a title-name entry and a given-name entry), fragmenting their claims, relationships, and chapter counts.
error_taxonomy.fixture_annotation: true_pairs carry taxonomy 'missing' (the class their failure takes if it recurs); false_pairs carry 'hallucinated' (the class of the claim itself). false_merge / false_split have no pair entries in this fixture; they are scored at roster level (see eval/README.md).
